CHIEF COMPLAINT: Burning with urination and urinary frequency for 2 days.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS: 24-year-old presents with dysuria, urinary frequency, and mild suprapubic discomfort. Denies fever, flank pain, or vaginal discharge.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS: Positive for dysuria and frequency. Negative for fever, flank pain, vaginal discharge, hematuria.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY: No chronic conditions, no prior urinary tract infections.

VITALS: BP 116/72, HR 74, Temp 98.4F, RR 14.

PHYSICAL EXAM: Mild suprapubic tenderness, no costovertebral angle tenderness, no distress.

ASSESSMENT: Uncomplicated urinary tract infection.

PLAN: Nitrofurantoin 5-day course, increased fluid intake, return if symptoms worsen or fever develops.
